items.evidence_text: The renal rule separates two actions: new treatment is not recommended at eGFR 30 to 45, whereas use is contraindicated below eGFR 30.
items.candidate_claim: A new patient with eGFR 34 falls in the range where initiation is not recommended.

items.evidence_text: Initiation is not recommended from eGFR 30 through 45; the contraindication begins only below 30.
items.candidate_claim: An eGFR of 34 meets the contraindication criterion.

items.evidence_text: When a person is already receiving the medicine and renal function declines below eGFR 45, the instruction is to reassess benefit versus risk; discontinuation is specified below 30.
items.candidate_claim: For an existing user whose eGFR is 41, reassessing benefit and risk is consistent with the evidence.

items.evidence_text: For patients already on therapy, eGFR below 45 triggers benefit-risk reassessment, while eGFR below 30 triggers discontinuation.
items.candidate_claim: An existing user at eGFR 41 must stop the medicine because the value is under 45.

items.evidence_text: Using an NSAID together with the anticoagulant can raise bleeding risk.
items.candidate_claim: The evidence supports a higher bleeding risk with concomitant NSAID exposure.

items.evidence_text: The interaction evidence describes increased bleeding risk with NSAIDs; it does not provide an absolute prohibition for every patient.
items.candidate_claim: This evidence establishes that NSAIDs are absolutely forbidden with the anticoagulant in all circumstances.

items.evidence_text: The medicine can precipitate a serious toxicity syndrome, and concomitant drugs acting on the same pathway can increase that risk.
items.candidate_claim: The source supports a possible toxicity risk, not a diagnosis in a particular patient.

items.evidence_text: The warning describes a syndrome that may occur and lists several symptom domains; the passage does not state that a single symptom confirms the diagnosis.
items.candidate_claim: One symptom by itself proves that the treated patient has the syndrome.

items.evidence_text: Spontaneous safety reports are useful for detecting possible safety signals, but they do not on their own demonstrate that the product caused the event.
items.candidate_claim: The report system can contribute to signal detection while causal attribution remains unproven.

items.evidence_text: A spontaneous report can raise a safety signal, but causal attribution is not established by that report alone.
items.candidate_claim: The report alone establishes that the drug caused the event.

items.evidence_text: Because spontaneous reporting is incomplete and subject to reporting biases, the number of reports is not a valid estimate of event incidence.
items.candidate_claim: The raw number of reports is sufficient to calculate the true incidence of the event.

items.evidence_text: The registry entry identifies a study as recruiting and records its prespecified primary endpoint. This evidence bundle contains no efficacy outcome.
items.candidate_claim: The registry supports the study status and the identity of the planned primary endpoint.

items.evidence_text: The registry documents study design and status but contains no result demonstrating clinical benefit.
items.candidate_claim: Registration of the study is enough to prove that the investigational treatment works clinically.

items.evidence_text: Guideline C supersedes Guideline B for current recommendations.
items.candidate_claim: Guideline C is the current recommendation source rather than Guideline B.

items.evidence_text: Guideline C supersedes Guideline B for current recommendations.
items.candidate_claim: Guideline B remains current even after Guideline C supersedes it.

items.evidence_text: A newly published randomized trial favors option X, but the current guideline has not been updated and continues to recommend option S.
items.candidate_claim: There is new trial evidence for X while the current guideline still recommends S in this snapshot.

items.evidence_text: A new randomized trial favors X; the guideline has not yet been revised and continues to recommend S.
items.candidate_claim: Publication of the trial automatically changes the current guideline recommendation from S to X.

items.evidence_text: Drug P inhibits CYP3A and Drug Q is a CYP3A substrate. The passage describes a plausible pharmacokinetic interaction pathway but contains no management instruction.
items.candidate_claim: A potential CYP3A-mediated pharmacokinetic interaction is supported by the mechanism evidence.

items.evidence_text: Drug P inhibits CYP3A and Drug Q is a CYP3A substrate; this passage contains no dose adjustment or contraindication instruction.
items.candidate_claim: The mechanism evidence alone proves that the combination is clinically contraindicated.

items.evidence_text: A genotype is associated with greater drug exposure, while this source provides no therapeutic dose recommendation.
items.candidate_claim: The source supports a pharmacokinetic association but leaves the dosing decision unresolved.

items.evidence_text: A genotype is associated with greater exposure; no therapeutic-management recommendation is given in this evidence entry.
items.candidate_claim: The exposure association alone proves that every carrier requires a dose reduction.

items.evidence_text: An observational cohort found an association between factor M and outcome N, and the authors explicitly state that the analysis does not establish that M causes N.
items.candidate_claim: The cohort establishes a causal effect of M on N.

items.evidence_text: Imaging describes the lesion as indeterminate and recommends MRI for additional characterization; no malignant diagnosis is made.
items.candidate_claim: The report supports calling the lesion indeterminate and recommends MRI characterization.

items.evidence_text: Two non-head-to-head trials report different response percentages in different populations, so the percentages are not a randomized direct comparison.
items.candidate_claim: The numerically larger response percentage alone proves treatment A is superior to treatment B.
